> If it’s based on RPM you could use the “ENTITY-MIB-SENSOR” (
> https://mibs.observium.org/mib/ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB/) standard MIB which
> allows to export RPM sensors via SNMP in a standardized way (any network
> monitoring system would be able to pick up these sensors without having to
> add some custom code for your switch models).
>
> Your custom working/not working and low/high speed logic is perfectly fine
> for us.
>
> In this case we would recommend to simply add it to your NMS-SYS mib (just
> like the power supply states).
>
> That will require some custom code for the monitoring systems but that’s
> no problem for us.
>
>
>
> I don’t know how BDCOM does the FAN monitoring but from our own experience
> with various hardware designs we would recommend using standard fan
> controller ICs.
>
> With industry standard PWM controlled and tachometer monitored fans you
> can use corresponding fan controller ICs available from all major chip
> vendors.
>
> In our own designs we use mostly fan controllers from microchip
> technology. E.g. for 2 fans the EMC2104, which is available for < 2 USD.
>
> Given that pretty much any microcontroller with PWM output support can be
> used using a low cost WCH CH32 microcontroller might allow further cost
> cutting.
>
> But for us at costs of ~1 USD per fan using a standard 4 wire fan
> controller (as they are used in pretty much any standard PC or server) is a
> no brainer decision.
>
> If someone asks for the cheapest possible switch you still can simply non
> populate the fan controller IC on the PCB and used simple unmonitored fixed
> speed 2 wire fans.
>
>
